evals.prompt: Record a decision: we chose PostgreSQL over MySQL for our primary store, after seriously considering MySQL and SQLite. The choice is costly to reverse (data migration). Write the ADR.
evals.expected_output: A full ADR following the six-section template, with every alternative carrying a `Rejected:` reason written in timeless language.
expectations: Creates `docs/decisions/NNNN-kebab-title.md` with a `# ADR-NNNN: <title>` H1
Status is `ACCEPTED` with a `## Date` in YYYY-MM-DD form
Records at least one seriously-considered alternative with a `Rejected:` line stating the specific reason, not 'worse'
Decision stated in imperative, timeless form
Does not invent a rejected alternative when none can be sourced

evals.prompt: Write an ADR for the decision to use 2-space indentation in the new module. The alternative (4-space) was not seriously evaluated.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses, names the failed eligibility condition, and writes no file.
expectations: Writes no ADR file
States which eligibility condition failed (no real seriously-considered alternative, and/or trivially reversible)
Treats refusal as a correct outcome, does not apologize or fabricate

evals.prompt: Record a decision in a repo that already has `docs/adr/ADR-004-Foo.rst` using headings Status/Context/Decision/Consequences only (no Alternatives Considered section), numbered sequentially.
evals.expected_output: Continues the existing scheme — `.rst`, the existing headings, the next number — and folds the rejected-alternatives content into Context.
expectations: Does NOT create `docs/decisions/0001-*.md`
Uses the existing `.rst` extension and heading set
Continues the numbering (ADR-005, not restarting at 1)
The rejected alternatives and their reasons still appear, folded under an 'Alternatives considered:' lead-in in Context
Narrates the adaptation

evals.prompt: A new decision reverses an existing `ACCEPTED` ADR: we are moving the cache from Redis back to in-memory. Write the new ADR that supersedes the old one.
evals.expected_output: Both the new ADR and an edit to the old ADR's Status, with both links present.
expectations: Writes a new ADR whose `## Status` carries a `Supersedes ADR-NNNN` line below its state token
Edits the old ADR's state token to `SUPERSEDED by ADR-MMMM`
Both edits happen together (no one-sided link)
Old ADR content (Decision/Context/Alternatives) is not rewritten

evals.prompt: `.adr-dir` points at `doc/adr` but the on-disk decision files live in `docs/decisions`. Record a new decision.
evals.expected_output: The skill surfaces the conflict and asks, without silently picking a location.
expectations: Detects the disagreement between config and on-disk files
Asks the user which convention to follow rather than silently choosing
Does not write any ADR before the conflict is resolved

evals.prompt: A multi-dimension Crucible design doc (4-5 `### Dn` sections, each with a `Rejected — …` block, in-house format) reaches the design hook. Multiple dimensions pass eligibility.
evals.expected_output: At most one ADR — the highest-rank dimension by the D1 tiebreak — with the rest declined-by-cap by name.
expectations: Writes at most one ADR
Picks the highest-rank dimension by the reversal-cost ordering (data migration > interface break > re-training > re-run)
Declines the rest by name, citing the cap, not an eligibility failure
Narrates the tiebreak when two dimensions fall in the same kind

evals.prompt: A design doc has two cap-eligible dimensions. Hook 1 already wrote one at design time; now the branch reaches finish with a diff that implements the second dimension.
evals.expected_output: Hook 2 writes the declined-by-cap dimension it now implements — two ADRs total across the whole build is the correct outcome, not a cap violation.
expectations: Recognizes the design-time ADR via idempotence and does not duplicate it
Writes (or re-declines) the second dimension only because the diff implements it
Does not treat 'one ADR per hook firing' as a whole-build ceiling of one
